title: Media dropped into the History workspace vanishes - it must become a history entry
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-562 - Dropping media onto History: the half-built handler and Composite Place (consolidation sweep 2026-08-14). Members and phase order: tasks/MPI-562/plan.md.

Drag an image into the History workspace and nothing visible happens: no new entry, nothing loads on the canvas. The file is not lost - it silently became a PROMPT CHIP, which the user only discovers after running an op and seeing their dropped image come out of the latents. Reported by the user as 'works as a bug'.

ROOT CAUSE, already located: MpiGroupHistoryBlock.js:913-921. The drop overlay's onDrop uploads the file and then does exactly one thing - `_pb?.el?.injectMedia?.(...)`. It never creates an item, never appends to history, never touches the history list, never loads the canvas. The drop overlay itself is fine; the handler is simply half a feature.

FIX: after uploadMediaFile, build the item (createImageItem / createVideoItem), appendToHistory, persist the group, historyList.appendEntry, viewer.loadEntry - the same sequence _runComposite already runs at 1881-1894 for its result. Copy that path rather than inventing one.

THE DESIGN CALL - entry AND chip, or entry only? The chip behaviour is LOAD-BEARING in video mode: dropping a start/end frame is how a user unlocks the frame-driven i2v ops when no media is staged (see the comments at ~217 and ~919), and `_isVideoPromptToolActive()` deliberately hands drops to the PromptBox while the video prompt tool is active. Do not strip the chip globally to fix an image-mode bug. Most likely answer: image drops create an entry AND stage the chip; video-mode prompt-tool drops keep today's chip-only behaviour.
acceptance: Dropping an image into the History workspace appends a visible history entry and loads it on the canvas
The dropped file still reaches generation as before - no regression to the existing chip staging
Video mode: dropping a start/end frame while the video prompt tool is active still unlocks the frame-driven i2v ops
Multi-file drops produce one entry per file, in drop order
A failed upload surfaces a toast instead of failing silently
The entry survives a reload - the group is persisted, not just appended in memory
